newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Joulwan urges Romania to foster PFP cooperation.
newsitem.headline: Joulwan urges Romania to foster PFP cooperation.

text.p: U.S. Army General George Joulwan, Supreme Allied Commander of NATO Forces in Europe, said on Thursday Romania should foster its Partnership for Peace (PFP) cooperation with the Western defence alliance.
But he declined to elaborate on the ex-communist country's chances of early admission to NATO.
"I would say Romania needs to continue its efforts and work in the PFP the same it has done so far," Joulwan said at the end of a two-day visit.

In January 1994 Romania was the first ex-Soviet bloc member to join the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation's PFP scheme of forging closer military ties with former Cold War foes. It has been an enthusiastic participant in PFP programmes.
Romania fears being left out of a first wave of admissions to NATO would leave it in a "grey area", sandwiched between the ex-Soviet Union and an expanded Western military alliance.
Last month NATO planners said they were developing a "super" PFP scheme, to embrace countries likely to be left out of the first wave of admissions.
Romania has peacekeeping battalions in various PFP operations, including an engineers' unit in the NATO-led IFOR peacekeeping mission in Bosnia.
Earlier on Thursday Joulwan had talks with Romanian President Ion Iliescu and Defence Minister Gheorghe Tinca.
